title: Platform safety is becoming a time-bounded removal and complaint-governance obligation
source_unit: FTC enforcement guidance and covered online platforms under Section 3 of the TAKE IT DOWN Act
geography: United States online platforms and people seeking removal of nonconsensual intimate images

denominator.unit: major platforms named in FTC compliance reminder letters; the statutory covered-platform universe is broader

request_deadline.value: covered platforms must provide a process for valid removal requests

removal_window.unit: hours after a valid request for the image and known identical copies

complaint_route.value: FTC launched TakeItDown.ftc.gov for complaints about missing platform processes or failures to remove valid content

observations.method: FTC enforcement announcement and business guidance describing the statutory deadline, removal duty, platform-process requirement, complaint route, and named-platform compliance reminder.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not report request volume, platform response rates, false positives, repeat appearance, survivor safety, or enforcement outcomes. A legal deadline is not evidence of completed removal or restored agency for any individual.
observations.subgroup: Victims and survivors of nonconsensual intimate-image distribution, including minors; covered online platforms.
observations.counterinterpretation: A centralized complaint route and hashing guidance may improve recourse, but access, reporting burden, privacy risk, platform implementation, and cross-border hosting can still limit practical protection.

related_sources.claim: FTC business guidance explains request identifiers and hashing to reduce reappearance of removed content.

boundary: This record adds a platform-governance and consumer-recourse mechanism: a harm previously handled through platform discretion is assigned a deadline, request protocol, and regulator complaint route. It does not show individual removal, safety, privacy, trust repair, or durable non-recurrence.
